You liked working with someone, then six months disappeared. You do not need an elaborate reason to get back in touch.

Try: “I was reminded of our conversation about onboarding when I saw this example. The section on first-week checklists made me think of your project. How did the new process work out?” Only send the link if it is genuinely relevant; a warm check-in can stand on its own.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Build relationships before you need them Networking works best when it begins long before you need something. The most valuable professional connections are built through genuine curiosity, generosity, and consistency. Reaching out without an immediate agenda builds trust that pays off later. Strong relationships are not transactional. They are built on mutual respect and shared value. Turn experiments into systems One of the biggest shifts that supports long-term growth is turning what works into a repeatable process. If a strategy produces results, whether it’s an outreach message, a content schedule, or a framework that resonates, document it and refine it. Systems multiply effort and ensure successes are not one-time events but foundations for future opportunities. Preparation isn’t about perfection. It’s about consistently building habits, relationships, and systems that position you for success when opportunity arrives. For more ideas on creating momentum and building opportunities over time, join my email newsletter at https://dorieclark.com/subscribe . Copyright 2026 Dorie Clark, all rights reserved.
